summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with 98.7 percent CGM coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries and no invalid or duplicate records. Overall metrics are acceptable: average 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent. The issue is the shape of the day rather than the overall level. In local time (BST, UTC+1) glucose rises from about 09:00, peaks in the afternoon (16:00 local average 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range), then falls into two hypoglycemia clusters: 18:00 to 19:00 local (19:00 local 15.3 percent below range) and 23:00 to 03:00 local (01:00 local 18.5 percent below range). Overall time below range is 5.1 percent. Across the whole period there are zero carb entries, zero e-carb entries and carbohydrates on board reported as zero in every sampled loop status, so the system operates fully in unannounced-meal mode with UAM and SMB providing all meal coverage. Loop statuses show a non-stock build with additional boost logic, insulin on board peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 units, and dynamic sensitivity values between 27.8 and 124.0 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile ISF anchor of 56. The most consistent explanation of the high-then-low pattern is reactive over-delivery with a long tail under a 10-hour DIA, not a single mis-set basal segment.

analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia is the dominant safety signal and it is time-clustered rather than diffuse. Evening cluster: 19:00 local 15.3 percent below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, 18:00 local 7.7 percent with a minimum of 42 mg/dL. Night cluster: 01:00 local 18.5 percent, 00:00 local 11.4 percent, 02:00 local 10.1 percent, 03:00 local 10.2 percent, 23:00 local 10.1 percent. Daytime hours 07:00 to 17:00 local are comparatively clean. Level 2 readings below 54 mg/dL occurred on 08-13 around 18:00 to 18:15 local (51, 47, 42, 45), on 08-14 around 19:05 to 19:15 local (48, 41, 41) and on 08-21 at 07:19 local (42). Two of the three sit in the evening cluster. Hyperglycemia is an afternoon phenomenon with 16:00 local at 32.1 percent above range and peaks of 285 to 293 mg/dL on 08-15 and 08-18. Insulin stacking is visible: insulin on board 4.73 units at 08-19 16:55 local with BG 262 and a 1.6 unit SMB, and 5.935 units at 08-21 22:10 local with BG 245.7 and a still-positive insulin requirement of 2.12 units. Against roughly 16.2 units of scheduled basal per day this is a large exposure. The 08-19 high is at least partly explained by a logged Occlusion and Pump Error at 14:40 local and should not be read as a settings defect.

analysis_steps.findings: The fasting-like window 03:00 to 08:00 local is the best-behaved part of the day: averages 104.7, 106.0, 104.2, 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with below-range falling from 10.2 to 0.0 percent and essentially no time above range. Glucose is flat to slightly rising, so the 0.6 then 0.7 at 05:00 then 0.8 at 06:00 ladder is not producing a fasting drift in either direction and there is no dawn pattern requiring more basal. The 00:00 to 03:00 local block runs on the same 0.6 U/h rate yet shows 11.4, 18.5 and 10.1 percent below range; because 21:00 to 23:00 local already declines from 120.0 to 105.7 mg/dL, this looks like carry-in from earlier insulin rather than steady-state basal excess, which is supported by the clean 03:00 to 06:00 hours on comparable rates. The afternoon 13:00 to 17:00 local block is the hyperglycemia core and overlaps the lowest scheduled basal of the day (0.5 U/h from 16:00), but the excursion shape is meal-shaped with carbohydrates on board at zero, so it cannot be classified as a basal defect. The evening 18:00 to 20:00 local block carries the highest below-range values while the profile raises basal from 0.5 to 0.6 at 18:00 and 0.7 at 19:00; this is the one place where scheduled shape and observed risk point in opposite directions, but it sits directly downstream of afternoon automation output. Targets are 90 mg/dL at 00:00, 100 at 08:00 and 90 at 23:00, yet loop statuses show effective targets of 80 to 116 mg/dL, so the profile target is frequently not the operative value. Temp basal activity is strongly bidirectional, with zero-rate temps of 10 to 55 minutes and high temps up to 3.6 to 4.0 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: The five carb ratio segments (13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U) are currently inert. With zero carb entries and carbohydrates on board at zero in every sampled status, carb ratio has never sized a bolus and appears only as the algorithm denominator, where loop-reported values of 10.5 to 13.3 match the profile segments and confirm the authoritative profile was the one running. ISF is a single flat 56 mg/dL per unit segment, but effective sensitivity is dynamic because dynamic_sensitivity_enabled is true with an adjustment factor of 70 percent and autosens_enabled is false. Observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit and is strongly BG-dependent, with roughly 108 to 124 at BG 84 to 98, 53 to 95 at BG 114 to 140 and 27.8 to 71 at BG 169 to 262. Two sampled statuses at nearly identical BG (124.1 and 135.1 mg/dL) show 83.0 versus 42.5 mg/dL per unit, which BG alone cannot explain and which implicates the rolling insulin term. Therapy response windows cannot isolate ISF: recorded boluses of 0.05 to 0.65 units are followed by changes of minus 108 to minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes, far beyond what 56 mg/dL per unit predicts, because concurrent SMB and high temp basal dominate. DIA of 10 hours with free_peak_oref means insulin on board decays slowly, which both inflates the reported insulin on board figures used to judge stacking and lengthens the tail into the evening and night hypoglycemia windows. Scheduled basal sums to 16.2 units per day, consistent with the profile name recorded in the profile switch on 08-13.

SMB and UAM are both enabled and are load-bearing: with zero carb entries they are the only mechanism providing meal coverage, so disabling either would remove all meal coverage. Under smb_always_enabled true the smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled flags are functionally inert; this is internally consistent but means an unrelated future change to the always flag would silently remove coverage. A material interaction exists: smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false while the period contains six temporary targets above 100 mg/dL, including 135 mg/dL for 180 minutes on 08-17 from 13:30 local and 180 minutes on 08-18 from 15:25 local, both inside the highest above-range hours, which makes afternoon coverage inconsistent between days by configuration rather than by meal size. The most material finding concerns SMB size. The configured caps are internally ordered correctly (15 minutes standard, 20 minutes UAM), but they do not bound delivered SMB in this build. At 08-19 16:54 local the basal segment is 0.5 U/h, so a 20-minute UAM allowance implies roughly 0.17 units, yet the loop text records UAM High Boost enacted with SMB equals 1.6 units while insulin on board was already 4.73 units. analysis_steps.findings: max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is inert rather than dangerous: the observed binding ceiling is 4 U/h, shown at 08-14 19:40 local where the text records an adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, which is consistent with the 0.8 U/h peak profile basal multiplied by the daily safety multiplier of 5.0. The highest temp basal observed anywhere is 3.6 to 4.0 U/h, so 12 U/h is never reached and lowering it would be cosmetic. max_iob_units of 25 is the material limit finding: against roughly 16.2 units of scheduled basal per day and 275.95 units of recorded insulin over 14 days, a 25 unit ceiling is on the order of one full day of insulin or more and is effectively not a functioning ceiling. The observed maximum insulin on board is 5.935 units at 08-21 22:10 local, at which point the loop still requested 2.12 more units at 4 U/h with sensitivity at 27.8 mg/dL per unit, and nothing in the configuration would have arrested further accumulation. The sensitivity group is internally coherent: dynamic sensitivity on with Autosens off is the correct mutually exclusive pairing, and the two Autosens target flags are inert while Autosens is off. Sensitivity ratios of 0.79 to 1.0 appear in the sample and are produced by the dynamic path; 1.0 is neutral. The dominant concern is dispersion and feedback: heavy afternoon dosing raises the rolling insulin term, dynamic sensitivity lowers effective ISF toward 27.8 to 42.5 mg/dL per unit, the loop doses harder, insulin on board reaches 4.7 to 5.9 units, and the tail under a 10-hour DIA lands in the evening and night hypoglycemia clusters. The dynamic adjustment factor of 70 percent is the single global scalar on this behaviour but is entangled with DIA and with SMB boost, so it cannot be moved in the same cycle as either. The carbohydrate absorption group is entirely inert because carbohydrates on board are zero throughout; min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 cannot be supported or refuted by any observation in this package.

Declared strategy and observed execution are therefore kept distinct: nothing is declared, and observed behaviour is fully unannounced. Observed execution is zero prebolus, zero immediate bolus and fully reactive UAM: 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 units averaging 0.42 units per entry, with no meal bolus, no carb correction and no extended entry in any exposed treatment record. The recurring excursion shape is consistent: morning rise 08:00 to 10:00 local peaking near 148.0 mg/dL at about two hours, and a midday to afternoon rise from 12:00 local peaking at 16:00 local at 162.8 mg/dL after roughly three to four hours with a total excursion of about six to seven hours, resolving into the 18:00 to 19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster. analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory was completed and produced three corrections to earlier reasoning. First, the afternoon hyperglycemia must not be attributed to the 0.5 U/h 16:00 basal segment: the excursions are meal-shaped, meals are never announced, and the loop reaches the 4 U/h safe ceiling and boosted SMB, a magnitude no basal segment change could or should supply. Second, the evening basal steps to 0.6 at 18:00 and 0.7 at 19:00 are demoted as a primary cause of the evening lows, because the 03:00 to 06:00 window runs on comparable and higher rates with almost no time below range, and because the evening insulin excess visible as 4.7 to 5.9 units of insulin on board is an order of magnitude larger than any basal step. Third, the overnight target of 90 mg/dL cannot be judged from profile values alone because effective targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL are being set by the build, so the profile target is not the operative value and a target change would not be separable from the automation effects. The competing explanations resolve into one ranked chain: unannounced afternoon meals drive UAM boost and maximum safe basal, the rolling insulin term rises, dynamic sensitivity falls toward 27.8 to 42.5 mg/dL per unit, dosing increases further, insulin on board peaks at 4.7 to 5.9 units, and the tail under a 10-hour DIA lands in the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 hypoglycemia clusters. Day-level confounders are datable and must not be averaged in: Occlusion and Pump Error on 08-19, temporary targets of 135 mg/dL on 08-17 and 08-18 that suppress SMB, a site change on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, a sensor change on 08-11 and 08-21, a profile switch on 08-13, and GLP-1 1.25 mg notes on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 with a roughly three-day cadence. The safest single first action is the one lever that is a pure ceiling with no interaction with basal, carb ratio, ISF, DIA or target and that acts only in the tail events preceding the documented level 2 lows: reducing max_iob from 25 units toward the observed operating range plus margin. Every profile row is held unchanged this cycle because each candidate profile change is either unsupported by data (carb ratio), not separately measurable (ISF, DIA), or confounded by automation output (basal, target).

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent and supports time-of-day analysis: 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, zero invalid, zero duplicate and zero out-of-period records, with a largest gap of only 65 minutes.
Overall glycemic metrics are good: time in range 86.0 percent, average glucose 121.6 mg/dL and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, which is below the commonly cited 36 percent stability threshold.

The fasting-like window 03:00 to 08:00 local is stable in both directions, with averages between 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL, essentially no time above range and time below range falling from 10.2 percent at 03:00 to 0.0 percent at 08:00, indicating the early-morning basal ladder is not producing drift.
Several individual days show strong control, including 08-08 at 95.5 percent, 08-09 at 96.5 percent and 08-20 at 90.6 percent time in range.

The profile is internally coherent and confirmed as the running configuration: carb ratio and ISF values quoted inside loop reason strings match the profile segments, and scheduled basal sums to 16.2 units per day, matching the profile name recorded at the 08-13 profile switch.
The sensitivity configuration is correctly paired, with dynamic sensitivity enabled and Autosens disabled rather than both active, and the two Autosens target flags left inert.

Device and therapy events are well annotated, with site changes, sensor changes, a profile switch, an occlusion and pump error, temporary targets and GLP-1 notes all timestamped, which allows confounded days to be identified rather than silently averaged in.
issues: Time below range is above target and concentrated in two clock windows. Overall time below range is 5.1 percent against a commonly cited 4 percent ceiling, and it is not evenly spread. In local time the 19:00 hour shows 15.3 percent below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, 18:00 shows 7.7 percent with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the 23:00 to 03:00 block shows 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent. Level 2 readings below 54 mg/dL occurred on 08-13 around 18:00 local, on 08-14 around 19:10 local and on 08-21 at 07:19 local.

Insulin on board reaches levels that are large relative to this patient's insulin scale. Sampled loop statuses show insulin on board of 4.73 units at 08-19 16:55 local and 5.935 units at 08-21 22:10 local, with the loop still requesting 2.12 further units in the second case. Against roughly 16.2 units of scheduled basal per day, this is a substantial exposure, and max_iob_units of 25 would not have arrested further accumulation.

Delivered SMB size is not bounded by the configured SMB caps in this build. At 08-19 16:54 local the active basal segment is 0.5 U/h, so a 20-minute UAM allowance implies roughly 0.17 units, yet the loop text records UAM High Boost enacted with SMB equals 1.6 units. At 08-07 22:16 local the text records standardMaxBolus 0.2 with 0.4 units microbolused. The boost logic appears multiplicative and is not represented in decision_inventory, so the configured value understates real SMB aggressiveness.

Afternoon hyperglycemia is driven by unannounced meals. The 13:00 to 17:00 local block carries the highest above-range values of the day, peaking at 16:00 local with an average of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range, with maxima of 293 mg/dL on 08-15 and 290 mg/dL on 08-18. Carb entries are zero for the entire period and carbohydrates on board are zero in every sampled loop status, so all meal coverage is reactive.

Effective sensitivity varies widely and shows a feedback character. Dynamic sensitivity values range from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile anchor of 56. Two sampled statuses at nearly identical glucose, 124.1 and 135.1 mg/dL, show 83.0 and 42.5 mg/dL per unit respectively, which glucose alone cannot explain and which points to the rolling insulin term amplifying dosing after a heavy afternoon.

Temporary targets above 100 mg/dL suppress SMB and make afternoon coverage inconsistent between days. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false while six temporary targets above 100 mg/dL occur in the period, including 135 mg/dL for 180 minutes from 13:30 local on 08-17 and for 180 minutes from 15:25 local on 08-18. The response window starting 08-17 13:30 local rises from 126 to 190 mg/dL by 180 minutes and falls only after the target expires.

DIA of 10 hours makes the insulin tail long and the insulin-on-board figure hard to interpret. With dia_hours of 10 and free_peak_oref, insulin on board decays slowly, which both inflates the reported values used to judge stacking and extends the active tail from afternoon dosing into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 hypoglycemia windows. No correction event free of concurrent SMB and temp basal exists, so DIA cannot be validated directly from this package.

Carb ratio segments have never been exercised. All five carb ratio segments remain untested because there is not one carb entry across 14 days. They appear only as the algorithm denominator in loop reason strings. Any change to them would be blind, and any future carb announcement makes them live for the first time.

recommendations.title: Primary: review the max IOB ceiling as the first and only change this cycle
recommendations.description: max_iob_units is currently 25 units while scheduled basal is roughly 16.2 units per day and the highest observed insulin on board across the sampled statuses is 5.935 units at 08-21 22:10 local, with a second peak of 4.73 units at 08-19 16:55 local. A ceiling of 25 units is on the order of a full day of insulin or more at this scale, so in practice it never engages. Because max_iob acts only as an upper bound, it does not alter routine dosing and does not interact with basal, carb ratio, ISF, DIA or target the way the SMB caps and the dynamic sensitivity factor do. Lowering it toward the observed operating range plus a clear margin would leave normal days untouched while providing a brake in exactly the tail events that precede the documented level 2 lows at 41 to 48 mg/dL on 08-13, 08-14 and 08-21. This is the least entangled lever available and is therefore proposed as the single change of this cycle. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 device statuses are exposed, so the true maximum insulin on board may exceed 5.935 units, and it is unresolved whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 includes temp basal, which affects the true total daily dose scale. For both reasons a conservative ceiling well above the observed peak is proposed rather than a tight one.

what_to_watch: Whether insulin on board still reaches 4 to 6 units on afternoon high days
Time below range in the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local windows
Whether the 13:00 to 17:00 local time above range worsens, which would indicate the ceiling is too tight

recommendations.title: Second cycle only: align the UAM SMB allowance with the standard SMB allowance
recommendations.description: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes is 20 while max_smb_basal_minutes is 15. The ordering is internally correct, but in this build the boost logic multiplies on top of the resulting bolus, so the minutes value still scales delivered SMB even though it does not cap it. Reducing the UAM allowance to match the standard allowance would scale boosted UAM microboluses down by roughly a quarter without touching any profile parameter. This is listed only because it changes the safe action order: it must follow the max_iob review and must not be applied in the same observation window, since both act on the same insulin exposure and combining them would make the effect of either unattributable.

suggested_change.precondition: Only after at least 10 days of observation following the max_iob change, and only if evening or overnight time below range has not already resolved.

recommendations.title: Begin logging carbohydrates for one recurring meal before any profile change is considered
recommendations.description: Across 14 days there is not one carb entry, not one meal bolus and not one e-carb entry, and carbohydrates on board are zero in every sampled loop status. This single gap is what forces carb ratio, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, the carbohydrate absorption settings and much of the ISF assessment to remain unverifiable. Logging carbohydrates with an accurate timestamp for the one recurring midday meal around 12:00 to 13:00 local, while changing nothing else, would make all of these measurable for the first time. It is an observational step rather than a settings change, so it can run alongside the max_iob review, but it should be understood that announcing carbohydrates makes the never-yet-exercised carb ratio segments live, which is a genuine new exposure rather than a neutral action.

suggested_change.target_meal: recurring midday meal at approximately 12:00 to 13:00 local
suggested_change.note: min_carbs_required_grams is 20, so entries below that threshold may not register as intended.

recommendations.title: Do not treat the overnight target as a lever until effective targets are understood
recommendations.description: The profile target of 90 mg/dL from 23:00 and 00:00 looks tight against 10.1 to 18.5 percent time below range in the 23:00 to 03:00 local block, but sampled loop statuses show effective targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL being set by the build rather than by the profile. Because the operative target is frequently not the profile value, raising the profile target would not reliably produce the intended effect and would confound the assessment of the max_iob change. This is included only to prevent it being actioned out of order.

suggested_change.note: Reassess only after the automation exposure changes have been evaluated and the relationship between profile target and effective target is clearer.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile rows unchanged this cycle, including DIA at 10 hours, and instead verify DIA with one targeted observation: identify an evening with no correction bolus, no SMB and no unannounced meal after roughly 20:00 local, and record how the reported insulin on board decays over the following 6 to 10 hours together with the glucose trace.
profile_recommendation.rationale: DIA is the profile parameter most likely to be contributing to the observed high-then-low pattern, because a 10-hour duration keeps afternoon insulin counted as active well into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local hypoglycemia clusters and simultaneously inflates the insulin-on-board figures of 4.73 and 5.935 units that are being used to judge stacking. However it cannot be changed responsibly yet. Every therapy response window in the package is contaminated by concurrent boosted SMB and temp basal up to 4 U/h, so no clean insulin decay curve exists: recorded boluses of 0.05 to 0.65 units are followed by changes of minus 108 to minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes, which is loop output rather than insulin action. DIA also interacts directly with dynamic sensitivity and with the SMB boost, so changing it in the same window as the proposed max_iob change would make neither effect attributable. The remaining profile rows are held for specific reasons: the five carb ratio segments have never sized a bolus because carb entries are zero; the flat ISF of 56 is only an anchor under dynamic sensitivity, whose effective values ranged from 27.8 to 124.0; the afternoon basal segments cannot be blamed for meal-shaped excursions while meals are unannounced; the early-morning basal ladder produces no fasting drift; and the targets are frequently overridden by effective targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.next_check: On an evening with no correction bolus, no SMB and no unannounced meal after approximately 20:00 local, record the reported insulin on board decay and the glucose trace over the following 6 to 10 hours. If glucose is flat while insulin on board is still reported above roughly 0.3 units many hours later, DIA becomes the supported next profile change; if glucose continues to fall while insulin on board reads near zero, the automation exposure rather than DIA remains the primary driver.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the 00:00 to 03:00 local hours run on this rate and show 11.4, 18.5 and 10.1 percent time below range, but the 03:00 to 06:00 local hours run on the same 0.6 rate and higher and show only 10.2, 3.0 and 4.8 percent falling to near zero, and the preceding 21:00 to 23:00 local hours already decline from 120.0 to 105.7 mg/dL. Uncertainty: this pattern is better explained as carry-in from afternoon and evening automation output, with insulin-on-board peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 units under a 10-hour DIA, than as steady-state basal excess. Dependencies: cannot be separated from the max_iob and SMB exposure changes; reassess only after those have been observed.

Evidence: the 05:00 and 06:00 local hours both average 99.5 mg/dL with 2.5 and 1.3 percent time below range and 0.0 percent above range, which is the most stable part of the entire day. Uncertainty: none material for this segment. Dependencies: none; no change is indicated in either direction.

Evidence: the 06:00 to 10:00 local block covered by this rate shows averages of 99.5, 110.5, 132.9 and 148.0 mg/dL with time below range of 1.3, 0.0, 0.0 and 1.2 percent, so there is no fasting drop and no dawn shortfall. Uncertainty: the rise from 08:00 onward coincides with the morning unannounced meal peaking at about two hours, so the higher values are meal-shaped rather than basal-driven. Dependencies: separating meal effect here requires the carbohydrate logging observation; until then no basal change is supportable.

Evidence: the 10:00 to 16:00 local block shows a progressive rise to 162.8 mg/dL with above-range values of 20.2, 7.5, 14.0, 16.6, 26.3 and 23.6 percent. Uncertainty: with zero carb entries and carbohydrates on board at zero in every sampled loop status, these excursions are meal-shaped and the loop already responds with boosted SMB and temp basal up to 4 U/h, a magnitude no basal segment change could supply. Dependencies: per the analysis rule, this must not be labelled a basal defect while unannounced meals remain a plausible explanation; blocked pending carbohydrate logging.

Evidence: this is the lowest scheduled rate of the day and it overlaps the highest above-range hour, 16:00 local at 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range, which superficially suggests an increase. Uncertainty: the same window contains 0.0 percent time below range at 16:00 but is immediately followed by 7.7 and 15.3 percent at 18:00 and 19:00 local, so adding basal here would push insulin directly into the constrained 17:00 to 02:00 window identified as the dominant safety signal. The 08-17 and 08-18 temporary targets of 135 mg/dL also suppressed SMB in this block, making the above-range figure partly a configuration artefact. Dependencies: blocked by the safety constraint and by the unresolved meal announcement question.

Uncertainty: the evening insulin excess visible as 4.73 and 5.935 units of insulin on board is an order of magnitude larger than this 0.1 U/h step, and the 03:00 to 06:00 hours on comparable rates are clean, so basal is demoted as a primary cause. Uncertainty: both of those episodes follow a large afternoon excursion and a boosted correction, including 0.2 units at 08-14 17:20 local followed by minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes, so the tail of afternoon dosing rather than the basal step is the leading explanation. Dependencies: this is the second candidate profile change after DIA, but only once the automation exposure change has been observed and only one at a time.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is an empty array and carbohydrates on board are zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so this segment has never sized a bolus and appears only as the algorithm denominator. Uncertainty: complete; there is no observation that could support or refute this value. Evidence: no carb entry exists in the 04:00 to 08:00 local window or anywhere else in the 14-day period; loop-reported carb ratio values of 11.1 confirm the segment is loaded but never exercised for a meal. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: blocked pending carbohydrate logging.

Evidence: the morning excursion from 08:00 to 10:00 local peaking near 148.0 mg/dL is handled entirely by reactive UAM with no carb entry, so no carb ratio effect can be observed. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: this is the second-most relevant segment for a future carbohydrate logging trial after the midday one; no change until measured.

Evidence: this is the strongest carb ratio of the day and covers the highest above-range hours, but with zero carb entries it has never produced a meal bolus. Uncertainty: complete; note that if carbohydrate logging begins, this strong ratio becomes live in exactly the window that already precedes the evening hypoglycemia cluster, which is a genuine new exposure to monitor rather than a neutral change. Evidence: no carb entry exists in the 20:00 to 24:00 local window; the 21:00 and 22:00 local hours show only a small rise to 120.0 and 127.6 mg/dL, insufficient to characterise as a distinct meal pattern. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: blocked pending carbohydrate logging.

Evidence: this single flat segment is only an anchor because dynamic_sensitivity_enabled is true with a 70 percent adjustment factor and autosens_enabled is false; observed effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, crossing the 56 anchor at roughly 130 to 150 mg/dL. Uncertainty: high. No clean ISF measurement exists because every recorded correction is contaminated by concurrent boosted SMB and temp basal, for example 0.2 units at 08-14 17:20 local followed by minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes where 56 mg/dL per unit predicts about minus 11. Dependencies: changing the anchor would shift the entire dynamic curve and is entangled with the dynamic adjustment factor and DIA; it must not be changed in the same cycle as the proposed max_iob change.

Evidence: the 00:00 to 03:00 local hours show 11.4, 18.5 and 10.1 percent time below range on this target, which superficially suggests raising it. Uncertainty: sampled loop statuses show effective targets between 80 and 116 mg/dL being set by the build rather than by the profile, so the profile value is frequently not operative and a change would not reliably produce the intended effect. Dependencies: confounded with the insulin carry-in from afternoon and evening dosing; must be reassessed only after the automation exposure change.

Evidence: the daytime block covered by this target shows the lowest hypoglycemia burden of the day, with 08:00 and 09:00 local at 0.0 percent below range, and above-range values that are meal-driven rather than target-driven. Uncertainty: low for this segment. Dependencies: none; no change indicated.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows 10.1 percent time below range and an average of 105.7 mg/dL on a 90 mg/dL target. Uncertainty: as with the 00:00 target, effective targets of 80 to 116 mg/dL observed in loop statuses mean the profile value is often overridden, and the declining trajectory into midnight is better explained by residual insulin from earlier dosing under a 10-hour DIA. Dependencies: raising this target would confound the evaluation of the proposed max_iob change and is therefore held.

Evidence: 10 hours with free_peak_oref keeps afternoon insulin counted as active into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local hypoglycemia clusters and inflates the insulin-on-board readings of 4.73 and 5.935 units used to judge stacking. This is the profile parameter most likely contributing to the observed pattern. Uncertainty: high, because no clean decay curve exists anywhere in the package; every therapy response window is contaminated by concurrent SMB and temp basal up to 4 U/h. Dependencies: DIA interacts directly with dynamic sensitivity and with SMB boost, so it must not be changed in the same observation window as the proposed max_iob change. It is designated the next profile change candidate and is paired with the specific verification described in profile_recommendation.

Evidence: both components are non-null and both are true, so verify is not permissible. With carb_entries at 0 and carbohydrates on board at zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, SMB and UAM are the only mechanism providing any meal coverage, and the loop demonstrably detects unannounced rises with deviations of plus 1.3 to plus 7.1. Uncertainty: low regarding whether they should remain enabled; disabling either would remove all meal coverage and would very likely worsen the 13:00 to 17:00 local above-range burden substantially. Dependencies: the problem identified is the magnitude and tail of SMB delivery, addressed through the max_iob and SMB allowance groups, not the existence of SMB or UAM.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all five components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. Under smb_always_enabled true, the smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled flags are functionally inert; this is internally consistent, though it means a future change to the always flag would silently remove coverage with carbohydrates present. A material interaction was identified: smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false combined with six temporary targets above 100 mg/dL, including 135 mg/dL for 180 minutes from 13:30 local on 08-17 and from 15:25 local on 08-18, suppresses SMB during the highest above-range hours, and the response window from 08-17 13:30 local rises from 126 to 190 mg/dL by 180 minutes before falling. Uncertainty: whether this custom build applies temporary-target SMB suppression exactly as stock oref1 is assumed rather than confirmed. Dependencies: enabling SMB with high temporary targets would add insulin into the constrained 17:00 to 02:00 local window and would contradict the dominant safety finding, so keep is the correct outcome despite the identified interaction.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all three components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. The ordering of 15 minutes standard below 20 minutes UAM is correct and both are conservative relative to common defaults. However the configured cap does not bound delivered SMB in this build: at 08-19 16:54 local with a 0.5 U/h basal segment the 20-minute allowance implies roughly 0.17 units, yet the text records UAM High Boost enacted with SMB equals 1.6 units, and at 08-07 22:16 local standardMaxBolus 0.2 accompanies 0.4 units microbolused. Uncertainty: the boost multiplier is not present in decision_inventory and is not adjustable through any supplied field, so reducing the minutes value would scale boosted SMB by roughly a quarter but would not cap it; confidence in the size of the benefit is therefore limited. Dependencies: this group and max_iob both act on the same insulin exposure, and the rule against changing dependent settings together means only one may move per observation window. max_iob is prioritised because it is a pure ceiling with no effect on routine dosing, so this group is kept this cycle and flagged as the sequence-position-two candidate.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: both components are non-null, so verify is not permissible and change is supported with explicit old and new values. max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is retained unchanged because it is demonstrably inert: the binding ceiling observed at 08-14 19:40 local is an adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, consistent with the 0.8 U/h peak profile basal and the daily safety multiplier of 5.0, and the highest temp basal seen anywhere is 3.6 to 4.0 U/h, so 12 U/h is never reached. max_iob_units changes from 25 U to 10 U because 25 units is roughly one full day of insulin or more against 16.2 units of scheduled basal per day and 275.95 units recorded over 14 days, and therefore never engages. The highest observed insulin on board is 5.935 units at 08-21 22:10 local, where the loop still requested 2.12 further units at 4 U/h with sensitivity at 27.8 mg/dL per unit and nothing in the configuration would have arrested accumulation; a second peak of 4.73 units occurred at 08-19 16:55 local and was followed by minus 168 mg/dL over 120 minutes. A 10 unit ceiling sits well above the observed operating range, leaves routine days untouched, and engages only in the tail events that precede the level 2 readings of 41 to 48 mg/dL on 08-13, 08-14 and 08-21. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 device statuses are exposed so the true peak may exceed 5.935 units, and it is unresolved whether total_insulin_u includes temp basal delivery, which affects the true total daily dose scale; a conservative rather than tight ceiling is proposed for both reasons. Dependencies: this is the least entangled available lever because a ceiling does not interact with basal, carb ratio, ISF, DIA or target, which is why it is the single change of this cycle; it must not be combined with the SMB allowance, the dynamic sensitivity factor, DIA or any basal segment.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: all five components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. The configuration is internally coherent, with dynamic sensitivity enabled and Autosens disabled as the correct mutually exclusive pairing and the two Autosens target flags inert while Autosens is off. Sensitivity ratios of 0.79 to 1.0 in the sample were read as neutral-to-mildly-sensitive current adjustments from the dynamic path, not as evidence of Autosens activity, and 1.0 was explicitly not read as disabled. The substantive finding is dispersion with a feedback character: effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, and two statuses at nearly identical glucose, 124.1 and 135.1 mg/dL, showed 83.0 and 42.5 mg/dL per unit, implicating the rolling insulin term rather than glucose alone. Uncertainty: high, and the unresolved question of whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 includes temp basal directly scales how aggressive this feedback actually is. Dependencies: the 70 percent factor, DIA of 10 hours and the SMB boost all modulate the same quantity, so it cannot be moved in the same cycle as either; it is designated the third-cycle candidate after max_iob and after the DIA verification.

Evidence: both components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. Both settings act only on carbohydrates-on-board decay and absorption modelling, and carbohydrates on board are zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses with zero carb entries and zero extended carb entries across 14 days, so both are entirely inert and no observation in the package can support or refute either. Uncertainty: as a conditional note only, meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 matches the observed midday excursion length of roughly six to seven hours well, while min_5m_carbimpact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes implies a fast minimum absorption relative to those slow excursions and could decay carbohydrates on board faster than reality once carbohydrates are announced. Dependencies: these become assessable only after the carbohydrate logging observation produces a real carbohydrates-on-board series; no change is supportable now.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Current operation is fully unannounced: no prebolus, no immediate bolus percentage, no carbohydrate or e-carb entry, with UAM and boosted SMB performing all meal work reactively. The single useful strategic step is to change information timing rather than any dose parameter: begin logging carbohydrates with an accurate timestamp for the one recurring midday meal around 12:00 to 13:00 local, while changing nothing else. Prebolus minutes and immediate bolus percentage cannot responsibly be proposed at any value yet, because no announced meal exists in the period against which either could be assessed, and proposing a number would be invention. SMB and UAM should remain enabled throughout, since smb_always_enabled is true and announcing carbohydrates therefore substitutes carbohydrate-driven prediction for unannounced-meal prediction rather than adding a second layer of dosing. E-carbs should not be introduced at this stage: the observed absorption profile of roughly three to four hours to peak and six to seven hours total is exactly the shape e-carbs address and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 already matches it, but with zero prior carbohydrate entries no e-carb amount, start offset or duration can be sized from meal-linked evidence, and no duration was inferred from any aggregate figure since average_extended_carb_duration_min is null. Note that announcing carbohydrates makes the never-yet-exercised carb ratio segments live for the first time, particularly 13.2 g/U at 08:00 and 10.5 g/U at 16:00, and that min_carbs_required_grams is 20.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The excursion shape is well supported by 98.7 percent CGM coverage over 14 days: the midday to afternoon pattern rises from 12:00 local, peaks at 16:00 local at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range, and resolves over roughly six to seven hours into the 18:00 to 19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster at 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range. Because meals are never announced, insulin necessarily arrives after the peak, which is the structural cause of the high-then-low chain rather than any single dose parameter being wrong. The user declaration is dated 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z but contains an empty meal_strategies array with strategy_stable_for_period null, so declared strategy and observed execution are reported separately: nothing is declared, and telemetry shows fully reactive operation. No conflict exists between them, but the absence of a declaration limits applicability and confidence rather than being resolved by inference.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrates, even as a rough estimate, with an accurate entry timestamp for the single recurring midday meal at approximately 12:00 to 13:00 local on 7 to 10 consecutive days while changing nothing else. This one observation simultaneously makes carb ratio measurable for the first time, creates a baseline for assessing prebolus timing and immediate bolus percentage, generates the carbohydrates-on-board series needed to judge min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours, and shows whether announcement alone reduces the boosted SMB and insulin-on-board peaks that precede the evening lows.

exceptions.pattern: Midday to afternoon excursion, approximately 12:00 to 17:00 local
exceptions.suggestion: Treat this as the single index meal for any carbohydrate logging trial, and record on each day whether a temporary target above 100 mg/dL was active, since smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false and SMB is suppressed during those periods.
exceptions.rationale: This is the slowest and largest recurring excursion, peaking at 16:00 local at 162.8 mg/dL after roughly three to four hours compared with about two hours for the morning pattern, showing 0.0 percent below range at the peak hour but terminating reliably in the 18:00 to 19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster. It is also the one window with an identified and datable configuration confounder: 135 mg/dL temporary targets ran for 180 minutes from 13:30 local on 08-17 and from 15:25 local on 08-18, and the response window beginning 08-17 13:30 local rose from 126 to 190 mg/dL before falling only after expiry.

exceptions.pattern: GLP-1 dosing days, 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 at 1.25 mg with an approximately three-day cadence
exceptions.suggestion: Flag these days as a separate stratum and exclude them from any averaged meal-response conclusion during the logging trial.
exceptions.rationale: Absorption is markedly delayed and prolonged on these days. The response window beginning 08-14 11:25 local, following a dose noted at 09:14 local, shows plus 135 mg/dL at 240 minutes and still plus 131 mg/dL at 360 minutes. 08-14 is simultaneously the worst above-range day at 20.8 percent and a high below-range day at 8.3 percent with two level 2 readings that evening, and 08-18, the day after the 08-17 dose, shows 12.8 percent below range with 15.3 percent above range. With a three-day cadence roughly one day in three is unrepresentative, which is a distinct mechanism from ordinary meal variation.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before any change: confirm with the care team that reviewing the max IOB ceiling is appropriate, and record the current baseline for comparison, specifically time below range of 5.1 percent overall, 15.3 percent at 19:00 local, 18.5 percent at 01:00 local, time in range 86.0 percent and the observed insulin-on-board peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 units.

Step 1, data clarification that requires no setting change: determine whether treatment_summary.total_insulin_u of 275.95 units includes temp basal delivery or only boluses and SMB. This single figure determines the true total daily dose, which scales both the max IOB judgement and the dynamic sensitivity interpretation, and it can be resolved without touching any parameter.
Step 2, the single change of this cycle: reduce max_iob_units from 25 U to 10 U and change nothing else. This is a ceiling only, so routine days should be unaffected. Observe for at least 10 days.

Step 3, during that same window, run the observational carbohydrate logging for the midday meal around 12:00 to 13:00 local. This is compatible with Step 2 because it changes no insulin-delivery setting, but be aware that it makes the carb ratio segments live for the first time and monitor accordingly.

Step 4, evaluate Step 2 and Step 3 together: check whether insulin on board still reaches 4 to 6 units on afternoon high days, whether time below range at 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local has fallen, and whether time above range at 13:00 to 17:00 local has worsened, which would indicate the ceiling is too tight.

Step 5, only if evening or overnight lows persist and only after Step 4 is complete: perform the DIA verification described in profile_recommendation by finding an evening with no correction bolus, no SMB and no unannounced meal after roughly 20:00 local and recording the insulin-on-board decay against the glucose trace over 6 to 10 hours.

Step 6, only after Step 5 and only one at a time: consider either reducing max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 to 15 minutes to align it with max_smb_basal_minutes, or adjusting DIA if Step 5 supported it. Do not do both in the same observation window.

Step 7, deferred to a later cycle: reconsider dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent only once max IOB, the SMB allowance and DIA have each been evaluated separately, because all three modulate the same insulin exposure and simultaneous changes would make none of them attributable.

Throughout: keep a dated note of confounders when reviewing results, specifically site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, the profile switch on 08-13, the occlusion and pump error on 08-19, temporary targets on 08-09, 08-15, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-20, and GLP-1 notes on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20.
education: Time in range of 86.0 percent and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent are both within commonly cited targets, so the pattern here is about the shape of the day rather than the overall level. Time below range of 5.1 percent against a commonly cited 4 percent ceiling is the one aggregate metric outside target, and the fact that it is concentrated in two clock windows rather than spread evenly is what makes it interpretable.

Hourly averages can hide the direction of a problem. The 16:00 local hour shows 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, while the 19:00 local hour shows 15.3 percent below range. Reading either hour in isolation would suggest opposite actions; reading them as one sequence suggests a single mechanism with a delayed consequence.

When carbohydrates are never entered, the loop operates entirely in unannounced-meal mode. Carbohydrates on board stay at zero, carb ratio never sizes a bolus, and the algorithm must detect a rise before it can respond. Insulin therefore arrives after the glucose peak by design, which tends to produce a high followed by a low rather than a smoothed curve.

With dynamic sensitivity enabled, the profile ISF value functions as an anchor rather than as the number actually used. In this package the anchor is 56 mg/dL per unit while the effective values observed ranged from 27.8 to 124.0. Two readings at nearly the same glucose showed 83.0 and 42.5, which indicates that recent insulin history, not only current glucose, is shaping the effective sensitivity.

A long duration of insulin action changes what an insulin-on-board number means. Under a 10-hour setting, the same reported units represent a longer and flatter remaining action than under a 5 or 6-hour setting, so both the interpretation of stacking and the timing of the tail shift accordingly.

A maximum IOB setting is a ceiling, not a dose. It does not change routine delivery; it only defines the point at which the system stops adding more. When the ceiling is set at roughly a full day of insulin, it never engages, and the system has no upper brake during the exact episodes where one would matter most.

Temporary targets above the profile target suppress SMB when the corresponding setting is disabled. That means two days with identical meals can show different glucose curves purely because a temporary target was active on one of them, which is a configuration effect rather than a physiological one and should be recorded when comparing days.

E-carbs are carbohydrate entries spread over time that shape the absorption model and carbohydrates on board. They are not the same as a pump extended or dual-wave bolus and they deliver no insulin themselves. Sizing them requires prior carbohydrate entries to compare against, which do not exist in this period.

Changing two settings that affect the same quantity at the same time makes it impossible to attribute any resulting change to either one. Sequential single changes with a defined observation window are slower but produce interpretable results.

Loop reason strings in this data indicate a non-stock build with additional boost logic. Some of the behaviour visible in the glucose curves originates from logic that is not exposed as an adjustable setting, which limits how much of the pattern any settings review can address.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice. Every proposed change must be independently verified with the care team before being applied, and nothing here should be applied to AAPS automatically.

Make one change at a time and allow a defined observation window before making the next. The analysis identified several settings that act on the same insulin exposure, so combining them would make the effect of any single change unattributable.

The dominant safety signal in this period is hypoglycemia clustered at 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local, including readings of 41, 42 and 47 mg/dL. Any change that could increase insulin exposure in the 17:00 to 02:00 local window should be treated with particular caution and discussed before implementation.

No carb ratio change is proposed because no carbohydrate has been entered in 14 days. If carbohydrate logging begins, the carb ratio segments become active for the first time, including the strong 10.5 g/U segment from 16:00 that covers the hours immediately preceding the evening hypoglycemia cluster; monitor closely during that trial.

Reducing max IOB is a ceiling change intended to limit accumulation in tail events. If time above range in the 13:00 to 17:00 local window worsens noticeably after the change, that would suggest the ceiling is too tight for this therapy and should be reviewed with the care team rather than left in place.

Several days in this period are confounded by documented events, including an occlusion and pump error on 08-19, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, a profile switch on 08-13 and GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20. Do not draw conclusions from those days without accounting for the event.

Keep hypoglycemia treatment readily available during any observation window, particularly in the evening and overnight hours identified above, and follow the care team's existing guidance for treating and recording low glucose.
